_comment: mem-reclaim policy. The boundary is the systemd USER cgroup, NOT process names (nix-wrapped binaries report unmatchable '.name-wrapped' comm). The user manager already splits session daemons (user@<uid>.service/session.slice/*: kwin, plasmashell, kded, powerdevil, …) from launched apps (.../app.slice/*: browser, electron, …). mem-reclaim kills ONLY app.slice members, and spares the app scope containing mem-reclaim itself (that scope holds the terminal + Claude + its MCP servers). So every KDE session daemon and the active Claude session are protected automatically. Curated 2026-06-28 from the live cgroup layout.

protect._only_note: A process is a kill candidate ONLY if its cgroup path contains this. Everything else (session.slice daemons, init.scope, user@.service root) is spared.
protect._active_note: The app scope (.scope/.service) containing mem-reclaim itself is never killed — terminal + Claude + MCP all live there.
protect._keep_note: Optional extra app scopes to spare, matched against the cgroup path (e.g. 'org.kde.dolphin|app-code'). Empty = kill every other app.slice scope.

signals._signals_note: SIGTERM all candidates, wait term_wait_s, then SIGKILL any survivor.
